data.description:
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker / tooling

#### Expected Behavior
merge-to-main.sh --resume should reliably resume driving its OWN staged PR (work -> staged-* -> main two-channel) after an interrupted run.

#### Actual Behavior
When the initial merge-to-main.sh run is stopped before it checkpoints its state file (here: the run backgrounded into wait-for-pr.sh polling a conflicting PR, then was stopped), --resume loses the PR number. Its GitHub fallback then resolved the WRONG PR — a pre-existing legacy umbrella PR (worktree->main, #534) instead of its own staged PR (#542) — promoted #534 to ready and tried to drive it, which can never pass check-staged-head (only staged-* heads may merge to main). A later --resume emitted 'ERROR: could not resolve PR number for polling phase'. Net: the two-channel promotion could not be driven by the script and had to be hand-driven via PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW + manual staged-branch sub-PRs. Workaround exists (hand-drive) but is costly. Fix: persist the staged PR number durably at creation (before any timeout-prone wait) so --resume re-binds to the correct PR, and have the GitHub fallback filter to PRs whose head is the session branch AND base is the script's staged-* branch (never a base=main umbrella PR). Observed with dso-dev 1.17.102 during the waxen-sigma session.
data.title: merge-to-main.sh: --resume after lost state file resolves wrong PR / 'could not resolve PR number for polling'
